Kremlin Removes Even Weak Opposition as Ukraine War Takes Toll
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
12:03:25 UTC
21:03:25 KST

Russia’s Supreme Court has removed Yabloko, the country’s only registered anti-war party, from September’s parliamentary election.
Despite the party having no seats in the State Duma, and only limited representation at the regional level, it still poses a threat to the Kremlin as Russian President Vladimir Putin and the ruling United Russia party’s ratings continue to slide.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
What happened to Yabloko
On Aug. 10, the Supreme Court annulled Yabloko’s registration for Russia’s Sept. 18-20 parliamentary election.
The ruling followed a lawsuit from the nationalist, pro-Kremlin Rodina party, which accused Yabloko of copyright violations, exceeding campaign-spending limits, and promoting positions that allegedly threatened Russia’s territorial integrity.
The Central Election Commission had approved Yabloko’s candidate lists only a month earlier.
Yabloko campaigned under slogans calling for a ceasefire, diplomacy, and an end to political repression. It was the only legally registered Russian party openly opposing the war.
Its campaign began generating unusual attention online. Videos showed young Russians holding apples – “yabloko” means “apple” in Russian – when asked how they intended to vote.
Several prominent exiled anti-Putin figures endorsed the party. On Aug. 6, Alexey Navalny’s widow, Yulia Navalnaya, said she believed it was “morally and politically right” to support Yabloko because of its anti-war position. Ilya Yashin and Vladimir Kara-Murza issued similar appeals.
Fires Erupt Across Russian-Occupied Crimea After Major Overnight Drone Attack
Yabloko chairman Nikolai Rybakov subsequently tried to distance the party from their support in court, apparently hoping to deny the authorities another justification for removing it.
He said people were backing Yabloko “simply because they want to live in Russia and don’t want to get killed.”
Hundreds of supporters gathered outside the Supreme Court during the hearing, demonstrating an unusual public display of dissent in wartime Russia.
From Yavlinsky to Navalny
Yabloko emerged in 1993, two years after the collapse of the Soviet Union, as the electoral bloc of Grigory Yavlinsky, Yury Boldyrev and Vladimir Lukin. Their surnames supplied the first three letters of its name.
Yavlinsky remains central to the party today as chairman of its Federal Political Committee. Yabloko was once a significant parliamentary liberal force but lost its national representation as Putin tightened his control over Russian politics in the 2000s.
Its history also overlaps with that of several other prominent Putin opponents.
Boris Nemtsov, who was assassinated near the Kremlin in 2015, was never a Yabloko member. He led the rival Union of Right Forces, or SPS, which attempted to form an alliance with Yabloko.
The two liberal parties repeatedly failed to unite, including during coalition talks ahead of the 2003 parliamentary election. Their rivalry became an early example of the Russian liberal opposition’s remarkable ability to fight itself while the authoritarian system consolidated around it.
Alexei Navalny, whose death in an Arctic penal colony in 2024 is believed to be another Kremlin-ordered murder, also began his political career in Yabloko. While the party expelled him in 2007, officially over his nationalist activities, Navalny argued that the real reason was his criticism of Yavlinsky and the party leadership, which he accused of suppressing internal opposition and refusing to cooperate with other democratic forces.
Navalnaya’s current support for Yabloko therefore carries a certain historical irony, demonstrating how little official political choice remains in Russia.
Genuine repression, genuine reasons for skepticism
The pressure on Yabloko is real.
Deputy party chairman Maxim Kruglov was sentenced in June to seven years in prison for social-media posts about civilian deaths in Bucha, Mariupol and elsewhere in Ukraine. Amnesty International described his conviction as punishment for peacefully opposing Russia’s aggression.
Boris Vishnevsky, another deputy chairman, was designated a “foreign agent” and forced to leave the St. Petersburg legislature. Lev Shlosberg faces several criminal cases and could receive up to 10 years in prison.
While these measures are not normally applied to completely obedient Kremlin puppets, Russia’s political party system is tightly managed. Political parties may formally exist, but the presidential administration decides which organizations are allowed meaningful access to national politics and how much opposition they may display.
A Kyiv Post source familiar with Russia’s political system described State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin as one of the principal gatekeepers for parties seeking to participate in national elections or have access to Putin.
In October 2023, Yavlinsky spent three days in quarantine before receiving a 90-minute meeting with Putin, during which he advocated a ceasefire, though in vain.
Yabloko’s record on Ukraine – just like that of most Russian anti-Putin activists, alive or dead, including Navalny whose stance on Crimea only shifted after the full-scale war – also deserves scrutiny.
In a 2024 interview with Putin’s goddaughter and sham opposition, Ksenia Sobchak, Shlosberg argued that Ukraine could not be described as ‘a victim’ because it was successfully fighting back.
The controversy surrounding his remarks encapsulated the Russian opposition’s ambiguous attitude toward Ukraine.
Parts of the Russian liberal opposition discuss the war primarily as a tragedy that must be stopped or as one man’s folly. In 2022, Former Deputy Energy Minister of the Russian Federation and Navalny’s associate Vladimir Milov described as “Putin shot himself not just in the foot, but also some vital organs.” Seldom is it viewed as an act of Russian imperial aggression that requires withdrawal, accountability and justice for Ukraine.
Why remove Yabloko now?
The crackdown matters because Russia’s war against Ukraine is taking an increasingly visible toll on Russian society.
In July, Russia’s state-linked Public Opinion Foundation recorded Putin’s sharpest weekly approval decline since the 2022 mobilization. His approval fell from 71% to 66%, while the state-run VTsIOM recorded a decline from 70.4% in mid-June to 65.1%.
Fuel shortages, economic anxiety, Ukrainian strikes inside Russia, and the war’s growing intrusion into daily life have made it more difficult for Russians to remain politically detached.
Levada Center polling subsequently found that support for the Russian military’s actions in Ukraine had fallen to 66%, its lowest level since the full-scale invasion began.
Support for Putin’s United Russia has also weakened. VTsIOM placed the party at 32.1% in its latest survey, down 1.4 percentage points in one week and 3.4 points from its June peak. Earlier in July, FOM recorded a three-point weekly fall to 33% – its lowest figure for the ruling party since the full-scale invasion began. By comparison, United Russia officially received 49.82% of the party-list vote in 2021, although polling figures and election results are not directly equivalent.
Even these figures should be treated cautiously.
Russian anti-war activist Daniil Chebykin previously told Kyiv Post that polling in an authoritarian state is distorted by fear, selective participation and survey methods that favor Kremlin-friendly respondents.
VTsIOM now conducts half of its political interviews by telephone and half through an in-person “route sample,” in which pollsters visit people at their homes.
“The respondent understands that the people asking the questions have his home address and other information,” Chebykin said. “Of course, he will not say: ‘No, I am against Putin. I am against the war.’”
Government critics may refuse to participate or provide the answer they consider safest. In-person polling may also disproportionately reach pensioners and habitual state-television viewers.
The real level of dissatisfaction could therefore be greater than the official numbers indicate.
Analyst Nikolay Petrov told the Associated Press that the Kremlin may initially have allowed Yabloko to run as an outlet for public frustration, expecting its traditionally poor result to demonstrate that anti-war Russians constituted an insignificant minority.
Instead, the campaign began attracting attention.
Navalnaya had warned of precisely this problem when she launched her campaign against United Russia in September 2025. Putin, she said, would use the election to claim that he was Russia and that all Russians supported him and his party, a statement increasingly challenged by reality.

Russian sanctions-proof payment system to benefit the world – top banker
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
12:02:57 UTC
21:02:57 KST

Russian sanctions-proof payment system to benefit the world – top banker
Russia has the capability to set up its own comprehensive cross-border payment network that would be domestic in origin, but international in function, the chairman of Promsvyazbank (PSB), Pyotr Fradkov, has said.
In October 2024, PSB launched the A7 system of international payments, which according to its website, now services 2,000 transactions of various sizes on a daily basis and already accounts for some 20% of all foreign trade settlements by Russian companies.
The creation of the system was a response to the sanctions placed on Russia by the US and EU after the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in February 2022, which included the disconnection of almost all of the country’s banks from the SWIFT global settlement network, Fradkov said in an interview with RBK on Monday.
After the restrictions were introduced, it became obvious that Western financial instruments “can be a tool for political pressure and influence,” the banker explained.
In such conditions, Russia “needs to create its own payment framework – domestic in origin, but international in function. We have plenty of both technical solutions and financial capabilities,” Fradkov insisted.
“PSB, together with the A7 cross-border payment system, is developing one of these projects for a new payment architecture where payment does not depend on the approval of a third party,” he said.
The goal of the A7 system is “to form our own payment infrastructure capable of conducting international operations independently of external restrictions,” the PSC chairman explained.
“The system is designed in such a way that, even after being sanctioned repeatedly, in various forms and types, the company continued its activities in processing payments for our clients,” he said.
Frabkov explained that from a legal point of view “no sanctions are being violated [by A7] because there is no such thing as a cross-border payment. It’s precisely that which has restrictions. There are distributed liquidity pools that exist worldwide in various currencies. If you take the jurisdiction of each individual country where we operate, then within it, this is absolutely normal, standard business that complies with all the regulations of that country.”
A7 is designed not only to bypass sanctions, but also be a competitive product on the international market that can be conveniently used by other countries to trade not only with Russia, but also with each other, he said.
According to the banker, it is important that Russia is “not unique” in developing a domestic settlement system as “many countries are following this path – Indonesia, Brazil, and others.”
“We are witnessing a global shift where the international payment infrastructure is beginning to be replaced by a list of national systems,” he noted.

Putin-backed BRICS grain exchange expected to exceed $1 trillion turnover
BRICS countries are working on setting up a grain exchange, backed by Russian President Vladimir Putin, that could challenge the hegemony of Western commodity exchanges over global agricultural trading and prices.
Russia presented the framework of the BRICS Grain Exchange at a meeting last week of the bloc’s economy and trade ministers in Jaipur, India, touting it as a “unified digital trading platform where producers and buyers of agricultural crops could deal with one another directly.”
Russia’s Union of Grain Exporters and Producers, which first proposed the establishment of the exchange in 2023, has estimated that trading of agricultural and related products could eventually exceed $1 trillion. Russia Unveils BRICS Grain Exchange Blueprint in Jaipur 
RT India dives a little deeper into the agri-trade model and why it matters 📹 pic.twitter.com/C866legEYh
BRICS countries contribute about 42% of the global agricultural and food output, and are home to more than two-thirds of the world’s small and marginal farmers.
However, global trading and price discovery in agricultural commodities is dominated by Western futures exchanges such as the Chicago Board of Trade and Euronext.
“The reduction of the number of intermediaries will directly influence the attractiveness of prices for all parties,” Ilyichev said. “Today, every additional link in the supply chain builds in its own margin. 21:01:10 KST

Over the course of a week, police officers, together with the Security Service of Ukraine and the Prosecutor General’s Office, inspected the infrastructure of fraudulent call centers whose operators posed as bankers, brokers, and law enforcement officers to gain access to people’s bank accounts.
"In total, 411 searches were conducted and the operations of 94 fraudulent call centers were stopped. Police found 1,794 fully equipped workstations in the premises. 26 suspects have already been notified of suspicion," the National Police reported in a statement on their website on Wednesday.
According to police, during the investigative actions, more than 3,000 units of computer equipment, 90 bank cards, access means to 20 crypto wallets, and 22 vehicles were seized.
"About $2 million, 64 thousand euros, cash in hryvnias, a kilogram of investment gold in bars, and jewelry were also seized," the report says.
Police emphasize that behind seemingly ordinary offices, officers uncovered an extensive infrastructure created for the systematic scamming of citizens.
"The schemes varied, but all were aimed at obtaining money or account access from victims," the statement specifies.
According to the National Police, in some cases operators called on behalf of banks to report alleged suspicious transactions or the threat of account blocking. In others, they introduced themselves as brokers and persuaded victims to invest in fictitious investment and cryptocurrency platforms. Some victims were promised help in recovering funds they had previously lost to fraudsters.
"People were persuaded to transfer funds to controlled accounts, apply for loans, disclose bank card details and confirmation codes, as well as install remote access software on their phones and computers," police noted.
In addition, certain call centers specialized in target searching for people interested in investing.
Another line of fraudulent activity uncovered by police was the sale of dietary supplements without a doctor’s prescription.
"The medicines themselves, by their chemical composition, possessed no therapeutic properties. Operators offered them to people as treatments for various diseases, although the products were sold without medical prescriptions or recommendations," the statement specifies.
According to the National Police, some call centers targeted foreign citizens. In particular, in one of the proceedings, Ukrainian police together with German colleagues are documenting the activities of a network that defrauded citizens of the European Union.
The suspects’ actions are classified depending on their role and circumstances of committing crimes, specifically under Part 4 and Part 5 of Article 190 and Part 3 of Article 209 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine – fraud and laundering of property obtained through crime. The maximum penalty for the charged crimes is up to 12 years of imprisonment with confiscation of property.
Currently, police are analyzing the seized equipment and financial transactions, identifying victims and the full extent of damages caused, as well as locating scheme organizers, other network participants, and individuals who facilitated the withdrawal and laundering of funds.

Lockheed Martin teams up to mass produce hypersonic weapons
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
12:00:48 UTC
21:00:48 KST

- Lockheed Martin and Albany Engineered Composites announced a teaming agreement on August 10, 2026 to scale production of U.S. hypersonic weapons programs.
- The partnership combines Lockheed Martin's systems integration with Albany's composite manufacturing to pursue future full-rate production contracts.
Two of America’s biggest defense manufacturers teamed up to solve a problem that has quietly threatened to undercut the Pentagon’s entire hypersonic weapons push, the country’s struggle to actually build these weapons fast enough once the engineering work is done.
Lockheed Martin and Albany Engineered Composites, a segment of Albany International Corp., announced a teaming agreement aimed at accelerating production of hypersonic weapons, systems designed to fly faster than Mach 5, or roughly 3,836 miles per hour (6,174 km/h), while maneuvering unpredictably enough to slip past traditional missile defenses.
Lockheed Martin brings decades of experience integrating complex weapons systems, the process of taking individual components like guidance software, propulsion and warheads and combining them into a single working weapon ready for deployment. Albany Engineered Composites, based in Rochester, New Hampshire, specializes in manufacturing advanced composite materials, lightweight, high-strength structures built from layered fibers rather than traditional metal, that can withstand the extreme heat and stress hypersonic vehicles generate as they streak through the atmosphere at more than five times the speed of sound. The companies said they plan to jointly pursue upcoming full-rate production contracts, the phase of a weapons program where a design moves from limited prototype numbers into the kind of high-volume manufacturing that actually arms military units in meaningful quantities.
Johnathon Caldwell, Lockheed Martin vice president and general manager of Strategic and Missile Defense Systems, framed the partnership as a direct response to Pentagon pressure to close the gap between hypersonic weapons that work in testing and hypersonic weapons the military can actually stockpile.
“By pairing our experience in system integration and battle-ready engineering with Albany’s cutting-edge composite production, we are accelerating the delivery of critical technologies to bolster the Arsenal of Freedom and strengthen our defense industrial base,” said Caldwell.
That reference to the Arsenal of Freedom points to a broader Pentagon manufacturing initiative pushing defense contractors toward faster, higher-volume production across multiple weapons categories, part of a wider effort under Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to reduce the years-long lag that has historically separated a weapon’s successful test flight from its actual availability on a battlefield. Chris Stone, president of Albany Engineered Composites, echoed that urgency while pointing specifically to the manufacturing bottleneck his company aims to help solve.
“The future of hypersonics depends on more than breakthrough design, it requires the ability to manufacture advanced composite structures at unprecedented scale. This partnership combines Lockheed Martin’s proven architecture with Albany’s advanced composite technologies and agile manufacturing capabilities to deliver a low-risk solution with the speed and quality the Department of War requires,” said Stone.
The urgency behind that manufacturing push reflects a strategic reality American defense planners have grown increasingly vocal about over the past year, that China has already moved its own hypersonic weapons from testing into fielded, combat-ready status. Chinese state media has reported that the country’s DF-17 hypersonic missile has reached full combat capability and entered mass deployment, a milestone that puts pressure on the United States to demonstrate it can not only design comparable technology but actually manufacture it in numbers that matter for deterrence, rather than producing a small handful of expensive, hand-built prototypes that take years to reach operational units.
The company recently disclosed a multimillion-dollar investment in what it calls its Modular Prompt Distributed Strike system, an approach built on flight-tested hypersonic technologies and an established industrial base, designed specifically to reduce the engineering rework and cost typically required to integrate new hypersonic payloads into existing airframes. Lockheed Martin has said that investment supports the Department of War’s Scaled Hypersonics Critical Technology Area, part of a broader munitions acceleration initiative, and that the modular design increases automation throughout assembly, integration and testing in order to cut labor hours and shorten delivery timelines. Those efforts sit alongside Lockheed Martin’s continued work on Conventional Prompt Strike, a major hypersonic weapons program the company’s CEO Jim Taiclet told investors during the company’s second-quarter 2026 earnings call had made continued technical and contractual progress following a series of successful flight tests, with $1.4 billion in contract modifications aimed at speeding the program’s development.
Neither Lockheed Martin nor Albany Engineered Composites disclosed the financial terms of this new teaming agreement, nor did they identify which specific hypersonic weapons programs the partnership will ultimately support once full-rate production opportunities are formally competed and awarded.
The companies did describe the agreement as built on a flexible structure with clearly defined roles and cost responsibilities between the two firms, a framework intended to let the partnership adapt quickly as Pentagon program requirements and government directives continue evolving, rather than locking both companies into a rigid arrangement that could become outdated as hypersonic weapons priorities shift.

BEIJING, Aug. 12 (Xinhua) -- The Yellow River, China's second-longest river, has maintained an uninterrupted flow for 27 consecutive years, the Ministry of Water Resources said Wednesday.
The Yellow River Conservancy Commission under the ministry launched unified water regulation for the river in 1999. Since then, water allocation operations have evolved from a basic goal of preventing dry-ups to a refined, multi-objective coordination system, becoming central to safeguarding the river's ecological health.
During the 2025-2026 period, total inflow from the main water-source areas of the Yellow River basin reached about 48.92 billion cubic meters, approximately 7 percent above the multi-year average.
For ecological water replenishment and inter-basin transfers, 346 million cubic meters of water was diverted from the Yellow River to Hebei Province in north China, providing a stable water source for the ecological restoration of river and lake systems in the region.
The first batch of 18 river restoration projects in the Yellow River basin has been fully completed. Moving forward, efforts to restore river and lake ecosystems will be further expanded, with a second batch of 29 rivers and lakes already added to the restoration list, the ministry said. ■

====================================================================================================

Humpbacks return to Rio: the whales are back from the brink of extinction – but will tourism help or hinder?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
12:00:28 UTC
21:00:28 KST

The anticipation is palpable onboard the Boaventura II as the yacht sets off from Rio de Janeiro at sunrise. Once beyond the Cagarras Islands, rocky outcrops just three miles off Ipanema beach, the group gathers at the bow and starts scanning the horizon.
They do not have to wait long. “Eleven o’clock!” someone calls out, as a pod of bottlenose dolphins appears, playfully diving in and out of the water. Then, two spouts of vapour hanging in the air signal the reason for the outing: a pair of humpback whales. The majestic mammals surface to breathe with an unhurried chuff, before revealing the underside of their fluke as they dive back underwater.
This is a bucket-list moment for many on the boat, heightened by the spectacular backdrop of Rio’s jungle-cloaked mountains. But such a sight has become increasingly common, as Brazil’s humpback whales return to the shores of the Cidade Maravilhosa (Marvellous City) during the southern hemisphere winter after making a remarkable comeback from near-extinction.
This year, one whale has even been repeatedly spotted within Rio’s Guanabara Bay. The sightings – at least 18 – are a first and have sparked speculation that humpbacks are returning to areas they once occupied centuries ago.
“You can’t put a price on this show. It’s pure magic,” says the yacht’s skipper, Theo Andrade, co-founder of the tour agency ROC Sail. After working on whale-watching expeditions around breeding grounds farther north, Andrade started running his own outings in Rio this year.
Luciane dos Santos, a 53-year-old passenger, is fascinated by the gentle giants and took a day out of her busy life running a drinks wholesaler in the hopes of catching a glimpse of them. “I’m amazed at how a 50-tonne animal can perform such a beautiful leap that leaves everyone spellbound,” she says.
She was not disappointed. “I feel a sense of fullness – it’s truly a gift from nature,” says Dos Santos, after a morning spent admiring six humpbacks performing their aquatic ballet.
Humpbacks have always travelled along the Brazilian coast between June and November as they migrate from feeding grounds around South Georgia and the Sandwich Islands in the South Atlantic to the warmer, shallower waters of the Abrolhos Bank, off Brazil’s north-east coast, to breed.
As elsewhere, indiscriminate hunting – recorded as early as about 1780 in Rio by the artist Leandro Joaquim, who painted scenes of whales being chased and harpooned in Guanabara Bay – had decimated the population by the time a global ban on commercial whaling took effect in 1986.
“At the end of the 1980s, fewer than 1,000 individuals were counted in this Brazilian group. Today, there are nearly 30,000,” says Thiago Ferrari, director of the Amigos da Jubarte (Friends of the Humpback) conservation project. Other estimates put the number closer to 35,000.
Brazilian waters are home to several whale species, including the once-endangered southern right whale – believed to be the species depicted in Joaquim’s painting – and Bryde’s whale. The 15-metre-long humpback is, however, “the star of the show” due to its acrobatic performances, says Ferrari.
Liliane Lodi, a marine biologist who works for the Ilhas do Rio (Islands of Rio) research project, which first registered a humpback whale in the city’s waters in 2014. The number of sightings has soared since then and, with them, observation of new and different behaviours.
“Rio de Janeiro is an area of passage; it’s a migration route,” she says of humpbacks. “However, we have already registered behaviour that is typical of breeding grounds, rather than passage areas.”
That includes spotting newborn calves, displays of competitive behaviour between males and recordings of haunting whale songs.
This year, Lodi has been investigating the Guanabara Bay appearances. She concluded that they are of the same whale – a juvenile that has been living in the bay’s sheltered waters since mid-June, delighting early-morning canoeists. “It’s very sociable when it wants to be,” says Lodi, who enlisted the help of citizen scientists to study the animal.
Such collaboration between science and leisure is one of the reasons advocates believe Rio’s budding whalewatching industry can be a tool for conservation, as well as a new source of tourism revenue during the winter.
Mariana Bueno is an environmental sciences student employed by ROC Sail to accompany each whalewatching outing on the Boaventura II. “When you combine tourism and research,” she says, “you have infinitely better data collection than if you weren’t working together.”
Having a researcher onboard, says Ferrari, is “fundamental for healthy, sustainable and orderly whale-watching tourism”. With its team of biologists, the Amigos da Jubarte non-profit environmental organisation offers free training courses in partnership with local authorities, through which they have already certified about 20 agencies for cetacean watching in Rio, including ROC Sail.
Clipboard in hand, Bueno answers tourists’ questions, advises the skipper to ensure that he follows best practice – such as keeping at least 100 metres from the whales and never spending more than 30 minutes near the same individuals – and writes down details of every sighting. All of the information is passed on to Amigos da Jubarte to help research.
“Surveying the number of individuals allows us to track population growth … and individual behaviour,” says Bueno. “How they’re interacting with a vessel or how curious they are about humans. These behavioural surveys then serve as the basis for formulating laws and rules.”
But while Lodi recognises tourism’s contribution to research, she worries about its impact on conservation, as the trend for whale watching in Rio means more boats are clustering around the whale migration corridor just beyond the Cagarras Islands.
“This population increase is a source of great happiness to us researchers. But with an increase in numbers comes an increase in [human-whale] conflicts,” she says.
“Fishing, tourism, large ships, chemical pollution and noise pollution, these are all challenges [and] threats,” she adds.
Although Brazil has relatively robust laws protecting whales – swimming with them is prohibited, for example – the legislation needs updating and requires better monitoring to guarantee enforcement, she argues.
“For a whale, it doesn’t make much difference that one operator follows best practice if the others aren’t doing so,” says Lodi. “We’re dealing with highly intelligent animals. If they’re being intensely bothered, there could be cumulative effects in the long run.”

How to use up parmesan rind to make pesto – recipe | Waste not
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
12:00:27 UTC
21:00:27 KST

Although parmesan rind is tough, it has just as much, if not more flavour than the cheese from inside the wheel itself. It can be used just as it is to flavour stock or risi e bisi (Venetian pea risotto), but grating it opens up a whole range of other uses, such as in my mac and cheese “rinds” and today’s parmesan rind pesto. The flavour is very powerful, though, so add it to taste: you may find that you need a lot less than you think you do.
Parmesan rind pesto
Parmesan rind is a powerful ingredient that creates a more flavourful and robust sauce that holds up especially well against big flavours such as wholegrain pastas or barbecued meat and vegetables. Pesto is quick to make whether you do so in a blender or with a pestle and mortar, but I find that the latter produces a more interesting texture and, if anything, a more powerful flavour, because all that crushing and bruising releases more flavour compounds and volatile oils than the sharp blade of a blender. That said, to make it in a blender, simply pulse-blend all the ingredients bar half the pine nuts, until the pesto is smooth but textural.
4 tbsp pine nuts
  1 small garlic clove, peeled
1 pinch coarse sea salt
  75g bunch fresh basil, including the stalks
2 tbsp finely grated parmesan rind – I use a Microplane
  100-150ml extra-virgin olive oil
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden brown, then tip out and leave to cool. Put the garlic and salt in a mortar and grind to a smooth puree. Work in half the pine nuts, crushing them into small pieces (save the rest to add at the end, for extra texture).
Grind in the basil a handful at a time, working quickly to preserve its vivid green colour, then pound in the grated parmesan rind.
Slowly grind in the extra-virgin olive oil, until the pesto is of a consistency that’s to your liking, then finish by stirring in the remaining whole pine nuts and adding more salt to taste, if need be.
Serve fresh, or keep in a sealed container in the fridge for up to two days.

From solar to AI: why China may be entering its ‘Go Global 3.0’ era
As a new wave of Chinese firms captures global demand for hi-tech goods, a new report highlights a strategic shift towards AI hardware and robotics
Chinese corporate expansion overseas is shifting from solar equipment to artificial intelligence-enabled industrial technology, with a new generation of companies targeting global markets from inception, according to analysts at Goldman Sachs.
“China has entered the ‘Go Global 3.0’ era,” wrote the investment bank’s team, led by Jacqueline Du, in a research note published on Tuesday.
The analysts said overseas demand was largely driven by global supply shortages outside China, which created an immediate need for Chinese suppliers, as well as products benefiting from new technology adoption cycles.
These humanoid robotics firms were helping create entirely new demand pools, according to the report, with Unitree establishing a global market lead.
The Hangzhou-based manufacturer shipped over 5,500 humanoid robots last year, far above three of its US rivals: Tesla, Figure AI and Agility Robotics. Each of those companies delivered about 150 units, according to data from technology research firm Omdia cited in the Goldman Sachs report.

Could the rise of left-wing Democrats reshape America’s policy on China?
As progressives ride a wave of victories in the primaries, a Chinese analyst says they might push for a more ‘inward-looking’ foreign policy
3-MIN READ3-MIN
7

The Democratic Party’s ascendant left wing is likely to push American foreign policy further “inward” and away from big-power rivalry, according to a Chinese political scientist.
Meng Weizhan, an assistant research professor at Fudan University’s Institute for Advanced Study in Social Sciences in Shanghai, also said it was time for Beijing to move away from the notion that all American political factions took a hard line on China.
The remarks come as progressive Democrats are riding a wave of victories in the primaries, gaining ground in deep-blue districts as well as swing states that could be key battlegrounds with Republicans in the coming midterm elections.
Abdul El-Sayed – who won the Democratic nomination for Michigan’s US Senate seat by a razor-thin margin last week – is a notable example. The progressive former public health official will face Republican candidate Mike Rogers in autumn.
In June, former New York City comptroller Brad Lander beat US representative Dan Goldman, while Democratic socialist Darializa Avila Chevalier unseated US representative Adriano Espaillat, with housing, public services, anti-corporate politics and Israel policy emerging as central campaign issues.
In Colorado’s first district, Democratic socialist Melat Kiros ousted Diana DeGette, a congressional incumbent of nearly three decades.

German Military Reactivates Five Former Barracks for New Conscription Model
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
12:00:04 UTC
21:00:04 KST

- Category
- World
German Military Reactivates Five Former Barracks for New Conscription Model
The German Ministry of Defence has initiated concrete preparatory steps to reactivate five former military properties across four federal states, Sicherheit & Verteidigung reported on August 11.
This aims to create vital accommodation and training capacities for future conscripts.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
The infrastructure expansion aligns with statements from Defense Minister Boris Pistorius, who confirmed that Germany is accelerating its military overhaul and preparing to raise defense spending to €162 billion ($186 billion) by 2029.
Noting that the German public increasingly supports rearmament and military service, Pistorius stressed that Germany must build a position of strength to deter potential Russian aggression, while pressing domestic defense contractors to overcome project delays and meet the military’s growing procurement needs.
In July, the ministry originally identified eight former military sites deemed particularly suitable for the country’s “New Military Service” framework. The government is now moving forward with five specific locations: the Graf-Stauffenberg Barracks in Sigmaringen, the Unteroffizier-Krüger Barracks in Kusel, the Kurpfalz Barracks in Speyer, the Kanaal-van-Wessem Barracks in Soest, and the former US Ray Barracks in Friedberg.
Several of these sites also include their former training grounds, such as the Ockstadt training area in Friedberg. All five properties are slated to be assigned to the Army, though a final stationing decision has not yet been officially finalized, according to Sicherheit & Verteidigung.
The driving force behind this infrastructure push is the planned personnel expansion of the German armed forces. By 2035, the Bundeswehr aims to maintain a force of at least 260,000 professional and temporary soldiers, alongside a robust force of 200,000 reservists
The New Military Service, which came into effect on January 1, 2026, is primarily designed to build up this reserve capacity. Since the beginning of the year, all 18-year-old men have been required to complete a mandatory military questionnaire, and the compulsory medical examination for the 2008 birth cohort is scheduled to begin on July 1, 2027.
Sicherheit & Verteidigung wrote that, to support this massive intake, 24 regional examination centers were recently established nationwide.
Because the resulting demand for accommodations, training facilities, and exercise areas far exceeds the military’s current real estate inventory, the defense ministry suspended the conversion of former military land for civilian use last year. The freeze affected 187 former properties managed by the Federal Agency for Real Estate Tasks, alongside dozens of other active and recently cleared sites.
Before any final decisions regarding military reactivation can be made, the ministry must conduct local dialogues with municipal leaders. These discussions have already taken place in Speyer, Kusel, and Sigmaringen, with the mutually agreed results set to be formalized in official letters of intent.
A similar meeting is scheduled for Soest in September, while talks regarding the Friedberg site are still pending, Sicherheit & Verteidigung wrote.
The situation in Friedberg is particularly complex because the sprawling 74-hectare grounds are currently designated for other municipal projects. The city had initially planned to convert the area into a mixed-use district for housing and commerce.
Furthermore, the local district has already invested approximately 13 million euros ($14.9 million) into renovating the former barracks to accommodate refugees. While local officials have signaled a willingness to cooperate with the Bundeswehr’s return, they have heavily emphasized the need for the federal government to reimburse these prior financial investments, Sicherheit & Verteidigung noted.
To help streamline these complex reclamations, the federal cabinet passed the Bundeswehr Infrastructure Acceleration Act in July 2026.
The legislation introduces a new military construction law that establishes an “overriding public interest” for specific defense projects, shortens planning deadlines, grants environmental exemptions, and expands the administrative powers of the military, Sicherheit & Verteidigung reported.
The draft law is currently awaiting final approval in the Bundestag.
German Inspector General Carsten Breuer had previously ordered the Bundeswehr to achieve full operational capability by 2029 to counter a potential Russian attack on NATO territory.
Funded through an easing of Germany’s constitutional debt brake, the directive prioritizes expanding air defenses, long-range precision strike capabilities, electronic warfare, and ammunition stockpiles following warnings that Russia could rebuild its forces to launch large-scale aggression by 2029.

Meta and Nvidia plant 'very firm flag' in open-weight AI race led by Chinese Labs
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
12:00:01 UTC
21:00:01 KST

Last month, American tech giants came together to urge policymakers not to place "premature restrictions" on open-weight AI models, even if they're from China. Now, two of those companies are making a concerted effort to compete by introducing their own open offerings.
Meta and Nvidia both released artificial intelligence models this week that are available for developers to download for free via the open-source ecosystem, a contrast to the popular proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic.
Open-source AI has become a contentious topic from Silicon Valley to Washington, D.C., with critics raising concerns about the potential national security risks of Chinese models, and of the AI training practice called distillation, which can be viewed as a form of intellectual property theft. Meanwhile, most of the industry's leading players contend that restricting use of the models would be to our own detriment and would place too much power in the hands of too few companies.
"The age of AI can be one of prosperity," the consortium of tech companies wrote in an open letter on July 24. "With the right choices, open weight AI can expand opportunity, strengthen competition, extend American technological leadership, mitigate risk, and ensure that the benefits of this extraordinary technology are shared broadly across our economy."
As for distillation, they call it "a widely used technique for model improvement, evaluation, and validation."
Meta on Monday unveiled Muse Glimmer as part of a strategy to release its most powerful AI models to the open-source community. CEO Mark Zuckerberg said the company would open the weights for its latest AI model, Muse Spark 1.2. Weights refer to the calculations and rules that determine how the AI works and behaves.
A day later, Nvidia debuted Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. The model stems from the company's Nemotron 3 family of models released in December. The chipmaker said its models are "truly open source," because the company publishes the related "training datasets, techniques, and model weights" for developers to inspect.
Both companies still have to prove there's an audience for their offerings in a market featuring popular models from Chinese AI labs like Moonshot AI and DeepSeek, as well as Alibaba's Qwen.
Box CEO Aaron Levie, one of the signatories of last month's letter, is optimistic. He said Zuckerberg's plan for Muse Spark 1.2 is a "very big deal" because it's a powerful model that rivals top foundation models from Anthropic and OpenAI. The models this week from Meta and Nvidia are smaller and intended to run on laptops for tasks like powering on-device digital agents.
"There's a very firm flag in the ground that America will have near-frontier open-source models," Levie said.
Meta has tried this route in the past with Llama. That was Zuckerberg's initial entry into the foundation AI market, but the release of Llama 4 in April 2025 left developers unimpressed. Meta followed by spending billions of dollars to overhaul its AI unit, installing Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang as the division's leader.
Recently, Wang's group has been rolling out proprietary models under the Muse branding to try and develop new revenue streams.
'Tremendous amount of potential'
Levie said that companies put off by using Chinese open-weight AI models would be more inclined to experiment with Meta's upcoming variant.
"You probably wouldn't be able to put a non-domestic open-source model in a major government agency, as an example, and you wouldn't be able to use it at very large banks most likely," Levie said. "If you think about the kind of use cases that now Muse can be used in, it actually opens up a tremendous amount of potential."
Still, Meta in particular faces some headwinds as it pursues yet another open-source strategy. Umesh Sachdev, CEO of business AI startup Uniphore, said Meta burned bridges with third-party developers when it shifted from open weight to proprietary AI models.
"I think it's going to take more than a 3,500 worded article from Zuck to convince developers," Sachdev said regarding Zuckerberg's accompanying manifesto this week. "The emotion of my developers at Uniphore, they almost feel betrayed."
But Sachdev said he's rooting for domestic companies to succeed, "because more competition will drive down token cost, and will drive up innovation, and it's always good for consumers."
It's a sentiment shared by Forrester analyst Charlie Dai. He called Meta's latest move "strategically important because it restores a major U.S. frontier AI vendor to the open ecosystem."
"Developers and enterprises will likely welcome Meta's shift back toward open weights because it improves transparency, customization, deployment flexibility, and data sovereignty," Dai said. Now, the company must "prove it can cultivate a durable ecosystem beyond releasing competitive models," he said.
WATCH: Meta's new AI model is a "positive development for the ecosystem."

Russian Ministry of Defense reports capture of nonexistent village in Kharkiv region
According to Ukrinform, the Center for Countering Disinformation under the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine reported this on Facebook.
“Russian propaganda outlets are actively spreading the Russian Ministry of Defense’s claim about the capture of the village of Shcherbakivka in the Kharkiv region. This is yet another typical example of Russian disinformation, through which Russian propaganda is attempting to create the illusion of a continuous, successful offensive by Russian troops on all fronts,” the statement reads.
The Center for Countering Disinformation emphasized that, in reality, the village of Shcherbakivka was decommissioned in 1997, as there were no residents left. As of 2026, no such settlement exists in Ukraine.
“The General Staff and the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation have previously made repeated official reports about the capture of various Ukrainian settlements, which did not correspond to reality. For example, Valery Gerasimov, chief of the Russian General Staff, has repeatedly claimed that Kupiansk and Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi had been fully captured, even though the Russians do not control these areas,” the CCD emphasized.
As reported by Ukrinform, Viktor Tregubov, a spokesperson for the Joint Forces Task Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, stated that the intensity of Russian attacks in the Kharkiv sector has increased in recent days.

Colombia earthquake: What makes some quakes so deadly?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
12:00:00 UTC
21:00:00 KST

Colombia earthquake: What makes some quakes so deadly?
As Colombia reels from one of the strongest earthquakes in its recorded history, which killed at least 250, just weeks after more than 6,000 deaths in twin quakes in neighbouring Venezuela, many turned to scientists to learn why this series of tremors was so deadly.
Moving plates
Colombia and Venezuela sit on the boundaries of several moving tectonic plates, whose slow, constant friction creates a build-up of energy that is periodically released, causing an earthquake.
German Prieto, a geologist at the National University of Colombia (UNAL), told Reuters that Colombia’s quake involved the Nazca plate sliding beneath the South American plate far beneath the Earth’s crust, which is just about 40km deep in the Andean region.
The US Geological Survey estimated the magnitude of the Aug 10 quake at 7.4, striking at a depth of 100km, versus the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitudes of Venezuela’s late June quakes, at a shallower depth of less than 20km.
The depth of the epicenter in Colombia’s quake sent tremors as far as Panama, but gave energy more room to dissipate, averting a far worse disaster.
“Colombia is a seismic country and we have to be prepared for these natural disasters,” Prieto said. “You can’t predict or prevent them, but their effects can be mitigated.”
Motion and magnitude
An earthquake’s magnitude is measured by a logarithmic scale that gets bigger with every unit, so that a quake of magnitude 7 is more than 30 times stronger than one of magnitude 6.
Colombia’s strongest earthquake, one of 8.8 magnitude that struck some 50km off the northern Ecuadorean coast in 1906, unleashing a powerful tsunami that killed hundreds, released 126 times more energy than Colombia’s latest quake.
Another factor is motion. The events in Colombia and Venezuela were strike-slip earthquakes, set off by the horizontal movements of Earth’s crust, leading to a type of shaking that is far more dangerous for buildings.
Major earthquakes can often also cause aftershocks, a grave risk for those returning to structures damaged by the first impact. Colombia had registered more than 100 aftershocks by the afternoon of Aug 11.
Both of Venezuela’s June earthquakes occurred along a separate fault, initial data shows. The second was larger, leading the US Geological Survey to classify the initial 7.2-magnitude quake as a “foreshock”.
Terrain and infrastructure
Countries particularly prone to earthquakes, such as Chile and Japan, enforce regulations to ensure buildings can withstand fierce shaking, with use of strong yet flexible designs that let them sway without snapping.
Informal housing or poor investment in engineering, however, can be devastating when quakes hit densely populated cities. The 2010 Haiti earthquake is estimated to have killed more than 300,000 at a cost equivalent to 120 per cent of the prior year’s gross domestic product.
Colombia began designing earthquake-resistant construction in the 1970s and adopted its first building code in 1984 after a destructive quake in Popayan. Its current code was established in 2010.
Prieto said location, materials and building code compliance are key to making earthquake-resistant cities, adding that he believed this week’s destruction should be studied to improve existing building regulations.
Another key factor is soft terrain. Mexico City, built on a dried-up lake bed, is vulnerable even to faraway earthquakes because of the amplifying effect of the soil structure.
Venezuela’s coastal area of La Guaira, built on soft, loose soil, was hard hit in June, as were Colombia’s western valleys this week.
Forward planning
Imposing costly and hard-to-implement building codes in areas rarely hit by serious quakes can be difficult, while region-specific risks are also tough to guard against, said Suzan van der Lee, a seismologist at Northwestern University.
“Our earthquake record is long, but not so long that we’ve seen every possible type of shaking,” she told Reuters. “We’re often surprised when earthquakes happen in ways we haven’t seen before.”
Building networks of seismic stations and sharing data across borders is key to help lower risks, van der Lee added.
“Global sharing of data is very, very important because most earthquakes occur on tectonic plate boundaries that are always near political and continental boundaries.” REUTERS

Deadly attack on Red Sea ship adds to global supply chain uncertainty
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12

21:00:00 KST

Deadly attack on Red Sea ship adds to global supply chain uncertainty
A strike on a merchant ship off the southern coast of Yemen that reportedly killed several seafarers on Tuesday threatens to reignite deep concerns about global trade, amid the ongoing Iran-US war that has choked shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
Key points
- Red Sea is a vital global trade route
- Even greater uncertainty for shipping
- Seafarers must be protected, says IMO
“It is with sadness and regret to know that, once again, innocent seafarers have lost their lives in an indefensible attack on international shipping. I offer my deepest condolences to the families of those involved,” said Arsenio Dominguez, head of the UN International Maritime Organization (IMO).
He added: “It is particularly troublesome that the most recent attack has taken place in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden area,” noting that continuing attacks on shipping “only serve to escalate tensions and threaten global supply chains on which everyone depends”.
Mr. Dominguez’s comments followed a strike on the deck cargo ship Tihamah, which has been attributed to Yemen’s Houthi fighters.
Yemen's years of strife
The non-state armed group – formally known as Ansar Allah and backed by Iran – has been battling Yemeni Government forces, who are backed by a Saudi Arabia-led coalition, for more than a decade.
The group has also threatened to blockade the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key shipping route to the Red Sea, and targeted shipping in the Red Sea for several years, including following the outbreak of the Hamas-Israel war in October 2023, in support of Palestinians in Gaza. On 23 July, they claimed to have struck two Saudi oil tankers, according to media reports.
Following those strikes, UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed deep alarm about the resumption of Houthi attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea and the renewed threats to maritime navigation.
According to online marine registries, the Tihamah sails under the flag of Tanzania; it is 62.8 metres long and 11 metres wide.
The Tihamah attack comes amid an ongoing near-total shipping freeze in the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway linking the wider world to multiple Gulf States, including Iran and Oman. Latest IMO data indicates that only around seven ships passed through the strait on Sunday, almost 20 times lower than the pre-war daily average.
The disruption to global trade in the strait that has followed US and Israeli strikes on Iran and counter-strikes by Tehran across Gulf States and Jordan has caused exports of key commodities such as oil, gas and fertilizer inputs to plunge – and prices to rise.
Evacuations on hold
The ongoing war has also forced the IMO-coordinated evacuation plan for seafarers stranded in or near the Strait of Hormuz to be put on hold. Some 6,000 crew members and 500 vessels are still believed to be trapped, almost six months since months since hostilities began, with around 2,900 individuals evacuated to date.
According to the UN agency’s tracker on the Hormuz crisis, there have been 65 confirmed incidents and 17 seafarers killed since early March.
In his statement, the IMO chief also called for the “immediate and unconditional release of all seafarers” held captive following piracy attacks in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden region.
“Ensuring seafarer safety is a fundamental obligation under international law and a shared responsibility of the global community,” Mr. Dominguez stressed.

Five years after Taliban takeover, Afghan women ‘erased from public life’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

Five years after Taliban takeover, Afghan women ‘erased from public life’
Five years after the Taliban seized power, women and girls in Afghanistan have been systematically stripped of their rights, UN agencies said on Wednesday. De facto authorities have issued more than 100 decrees curbing education, work and freedom of movement – restrictions now compounded by deep cuts to aid on the ground.
Key points
- The Talban have issued more than 100 decrees targeting women and girls, including one that’s left 2.4 million girls excluded from secondary education
- Unprecedented restrictions have triggered a mental health crisis
- UN culture agency, UNESCO, calls for the full restoration of the right to education
In the past year alone, this exclusion of women and girls from education, employment, public life, justice systems and healthcare has only intensified, entrenching what remains the “world’s most severe women’s rights crisis”, the organization’s gender equality agency UN Women said.
‘Devastating’ impact
“The results are devastating,” the agency added, stressing that shorter life expectancy, higher risks of maternal death, child marriage and gender-based violence alongside the loss of education, work and freedom of movement have also triggered a mental health crisis.
Over the past five years, restrictive decrees targeting women and girls have institutionalised discrimination and stripped them of their fundamental rights, with profound consequences for their lives and communities, according to new UN Women data.
Read the full report here.
Shut in
Half of Afghan women interviewed leave home only once or twice a month because of the severe restrictions on their movement and access to public spaces, according to UN Women.
In addition, more women are also reporting feeling unsafe leaving home without a male guardian.
“This unparalleled crisis of women’s and girls’ rights is at risk of being forgotten by the world,” the agency said.
Shut out
As of 2026, an estimated 2.4 million girls remain excluded from secondary education, with restrictions reversing two decades of progress in expanding access to education.
“Afghanistan is the only country in the world to formally prohibit access to education for girls and women beyond the primary level,” UNESCO said in a statement.
“The continued exclusion of girls and women from education constitutes a grave violation of their fundamental human right to learn and risks condemning Afghanistan to decades of lost potential, deepening poverty, and irreversible harm.”
‘Erased from public life’
Barred from secondary school and university and excluded from most paid work, women also face legal barriers to protect them against all forms of violence, UNESCO said.
“Women have been erased from public life,” the UN agency said. “As a new generation of girls grows without an education, their future becomes increasingly dark.”
UNESCO called for the full restoration of the right to education for Afghan girls and women, echoing entreaties from many UN agencies and leaders to protect and promote their human rights.
Stark funding cuts
UN agencies are reporting that the global aid cutback trend have taken a toll on the ground in Afghanistan, with UN Women stating that nearly three-quarters of women-led organizations surveyed in Afghanistan experienced funding cuts in 2025.
UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Afghanistan Bruno Lemarquis said funding gaps could, among other things, force health centre closures, “leaving thousands of mothers and newborns vulnerable to preventable complications and death”.
Meanwhile, the UN World Food Programme warned last week that devastating funding cuts will affect food deliveries to the most hungry at a time when a hunger crisis is affecting 14 million Afghans.
What’s the UN doing?
Here’s a snapshot of how agencies are supporting Afghans:
- UN Women: Efforts include bolstering livelihoods, helping safeguard access to lifesaving services and supporting nearly 200 women-led civil society organisations
- UNESCO: Activities include improving education quality and providing community-based livelihood and vocational skills training opportunities
- The UN sexual and reproductive health agency, UNFPA: Support for such initiatives as mid-wife training and Family Health Houses, which save lives in hard-to-reach areas
- UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF): From lifesaving vaccinations to building schools, efforts also support such emergency assistance as the response to recent deadly flash floods

Erdoğan casts new regional defense pact as ‘historic responsibility’
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
11:59:19 UTC
20:59:19 KST

President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan has said a new defense agreement between Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan reflects a “grave historical responsibility” to help secure the Middle East, while insisting the pact is not directed against any country.
“The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement is the fruit of this understanding; it goes beyond being a mere consensus among the three countries to become an initiative for us to assume a grave historical responsibility in achieving stability for the region and providing security and safety for its sisterly and friendly peoples,” Erdoğan said in written responses to questions from Asharq Al-Awsat.
He said the defense deal, signed with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif last week, should not be viewed simply as a response to rising tensions between the United States and Iran.
The agreement marked a first step toward greater regional ownership of security and could eventually expand to include other countries, he added.
Erdoğan said regional countries had to take greater responsibility for their own security, arguing that “no one knows the issues of the region better than its own nations and peoples.” He said Türkiye would continue to assume its responsibilities and pursue diplomatic efforts to strengthen peace and stability.
The agreement is based on collective defense, with a threat to one signatory considered a security threat to the others, Erdoğan said, but stressed that its purpose was primarily deterrence and regional stability rather than military confrontation.
“The primary goal of this agreement is to enhance its deterrent dimension, fortify the security incentive of the parties by strengthening the spirit of solidarity among them, and protect regional stability,” he said.
Erdoğan also rejected the idea that the pact was an immediate reaction to tensions between Washington and Tehran.
“There is no doubt that the rising tension between the U.S. and Iran poses a danger to developments in the region,” he said, adding that reducing the agreement to a response to that escalation would give an incorrect picture of Türkiye’s intentions.
He said the pact reaffirmed the right to self-defense under Article 51 of the U.N. Charter and was open to other “sisterly nations” that wanted to join.
Erdoğan also called for an immediate halt to Israeli attacks on Lebanon and said Syria had entered “a new phase” following years of war and instability.
“Our most important aspiration is for this phase to pave the way for a lasting peace, stability and the reconstruction of Syria,” he said.
Meanwhile, Erdoğan reiterated that Türkiye would not tolerate organizations or entities in northern Syria or elsewhere in the country that threaten Turkish national security.
“Just as Syria’s territorial integrity holds immense importance for us, Turkish national security carries the exact same level of importance,” he said.
On Lebanon, Erdoğan said the country’s sovereignty, political unity and territorial integrity must be preserved, and urged an end to Israeli military operations. He said ongoing ceasefire talks were a positive development.
He also linked regional security to global economic stability, particularly because of the importance of the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz to energy supplies and international trade.
Erdoğan said the countries of the region bore a “great responsibility” for maintaining the security of the waterway and called for restraint and diplomacy to restore the strait to a safe and stable condition.

Russian President Vladimir Putin’s visit to Novosibirsk this week was followed by an unusual development: petrol prices at some local filling stations reportedly dropped sharply – only to be expected to rise again once he left.
Putin traveled to the Siberian city on Tuesday to visit new facilities at Novosibirsk State University.

During his visit, petrol stations reportedly switched off price displays, while some temporarily stopped selling fuel, according to Russian outlet Vot Tak.
“When the president passes through, gas prices go down, but as soon as he passes, they immediately go up by 20 rubles ($0.24),” Novosibirsk resident Kristina S. told Vot Tak.
The reported drop comes as Russia faces mounting fuel shortages and soaring petrol prices, partly driven by repeated Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
Fuel shortages have already forced some Russian regions to impose restrictions on motorists, while long lines have formed outside filling stations.
Roads Fixed, Fuel Prices Cut for Putin
Putin’s visit also triggered a security and infrastructure blitz across Novosibirsk.
Officials reportedly ordered residents living along the presidential motorcade route to stay indoors and away from windows. Road closures caused major traffic jams, according to local residents.
Authorities also carried out road repairs and landscaping ahead of the visit.
“I wish [Putin] had just toured Russia nonstop. At least they’d fix the roads,” one resident told Vot Tak.

Iran not acted outside international law: Pezeshkian

HRW Urges US Congress to Block Turkey's Cluster Munitions Transfer to Ukraine
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
11:57:14 UTC
20:57:14 KST

Human Rights Watch (HRW) has urged the US Congress to block Turkey’s proposed transfer of tens of thousands of US-origin cluster munitions to Ukraine, warning that the weapons pose a long-term threat to civilians.
The rights organization made the appeal on Wednesday, Aug. 12, after the US State Department notified Congress of Turkey’s proposed $256 million transfer of 12 M270 launchers and several types of cluster munitions to Ukraine.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“Dumping obsolete cluster munitions into a conflict creates a humanitarian liability for civilians that is tragically foreseeable,” Nicole Widdersheim, HRW’s deputy Washington director, said.
According to HRW, the proposed transfer includes 70 M39 ATACMS ballistic missiles, 2,524 M26 rockets, and 47,000 M509A1 203mm artillery projectiles.
Together, the weapons contain more than 10 million explosive submunitions.
The proposed transfer includes:
- 70 M39 ATACMS missiles, each containing 950 M74 submunitions, for a total of 66,500;
- 2,524 M26 rockets, each containing 644 M77 DPICM submunitions, totaling 1.6 million;
- 47,000 M509A1 artillery projectiles, each containing 180 M42 DPICM submunitions, totaling 8.5 million.
The weapons have been held in Turkish stockpiles for decades and were originally produced partly by Turkey under US licenses dating back to 1987, according to HRW.
HRW said cluster munitions are particularly dangerous because they disperse numerous explosive submunitions over a wide area and can leave unexploded remnants that continue to threaten civilians after fighting ends.
The organization noted that 112 countries have joined the Convention on Cluster Munitions, which bans the use, production, transfer, and stockpiling of the weapons.
Trump’s Envoys’ Kyiv Visit Will Embarrass Them & Offend Ukrainians | Bohdan Nahaylo
“These types of cluster munitions are notorious for their record of not hitting their targets and hurting civilians,” Widdersheim said. “They should never be used.”
HRW argued that the use of cluster munitions can be difficult to reconcile with the prohibition on indiscriminate attacks against civilians and may constitute a war crime in certain circumstances.
The US is not a party to the Convention on Cluster Munitions, but Congress has imposed restrictions on the export of cluster munitions through annual defense legislation since 2009.
HRW said previous administrations have been able to bypass those restrictions by invoking a provision allowing the president to determine that such security assistance is “vital to the security interests of the United States.”
It remains unclear whether the Trump administration has made such a determination for the proposed Turkish transfer.
Congress can review the deal and pass a Joint Resolution of Disapproval to block it, HRW said.
The US State Department has notified Congress of a proposed transfer of US-made weapons from Turkey to Ukraine. Published in the Congressional Record on Aug. 6, the massive package includes 70 M39 ATACMS ballistic missiles, 12 M270 MLRS launchers, and thousands of cluster munitions.
The transfer, handled by Turkish, Bulgarian, and US logistics firms, is pending congressional review.
The notification said Ukraine seeks the weapons to strengthen its offensive and defensive fire-support capabilities as it fights Russia’s full-scale invasion.
The proposed package also includes 12 M270 multiple launch rocket system launchers, which can fire both rockets and ATACMS missiles.
The US government has said it is prepared to authorize the transfer following the congressional notification process.

Perseid meteor shower to light up night skies across Türkiye
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
11:56:54 UTC
20:56:54 KST

Perseid meteor shower to light up night skies across Türkiye
Annual meteor display will be visible nationwide overnight Wednesday into Thursday
Beril Canakci
12 August 2026•Update: 12 August 2026
ISTANBUL
Stargazers across Türkiye and the Northern Hemisphere are preparing to witness the peak of the annual Perseid meteor shower overnight on Wednesday, benefiting from unusually dark sky conditions created by a new moon.
The Perseids are caused by Earth passing through debris left by comet Swift-Tuttle. Tiny particles burn up in the atmosphere at high speed, producing bright streaks commonly called shooting stars.
In Türkiye, astronomers expect optimal viewing conditions between 2:00 a.m. (2300GMT) and sunrise on Thursday.
Observers are advised to head away from city lights to locations with clear horizons. No special equipment is needed.
Under ideal conditions, up to about 100 Perseid meteors could be visible per hour during the peak, although actual numbers depend on weather, light pollution and observing conditions.
The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TUBITAK) is also holding its 28th Sky Observation Event at Emre Lake in the western province of Afyonkarahisar from Aug. 12-15. Hundreds of visitors gathered in the region for expert-led telescope sessions and dedicated Perseid stargazing.
The Perseids remain active through late August, but the night of Aug. 12-13 is the main viewing period this year.
The meteor shower's peak coincides with another major astronomical event Wednesday: a total solar eclipse.

Isamaa and Center Party to meet with rector Tiit Land
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12

55 signatures and counting for Ülle Madise's presidential bid; parties meet with Land, Madise
Isamaa and Center Party held meetings with a potential presidential candidate, TalTech Rector Tiit Land on Wednesday. Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise will meet Isamaa, Center Party and Social Democrats on Monday.
Center Party representatives will meet Madise on Monday, party communications chief Andres Kalvik said. The Social Democrats have also scheduled a meeting for the same day, confirmed party communications head Ann‑Marii Nergi. Madise will also meet with Isamaa.
Riigikogu deputy speaker Toomas Kivimägi (Reform Party) said that collecting signatures for Madise began at 12:45 p.m. Wednesday, and she currently has 55.
Those who have signed include members of the Reform Party, Estonia 200 and Social Democratic factions. Kivimägi noted that signatures from Isamaa are not expected yet, as they want to meet the potential presidential candidate before deciding.
"From the standpoint of candidacy, this does not hinder anything, because 21 signatures is the minimum," he added. Kivimägi said Isamaa and the Centre Party have until August 21 to give signatures supporting Madise's candidacy.
Kivimägi said his goal is to gather more than 51 signatures by Wednesday evening. "I admit this is not the number needed to be elected in parliament, but getting 51 signatures in a little more than 24 hours is, in my view, quite an impressive statement," he said.
Kivimägi emphasized that he is not convinced whether Isamaa is ready to support any particular presidential candidate in parliament. "Perhaps that will change," he added.
Isamaa met Tallinn University of Technology Rector Tiit Land on Wednesday afternoon.
Isamaa chair Urmas Reinsalu said in an interview that the meeting with Land was genuine and honest. "On Monday we will meet with Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, this time already in the role of a candidate," he added.
Reinsalu said that once Monday's meeting with Madise has taken place, all the most significant candidates will have been heard. After that, Isamaa can make its decision.
Land said that various topics were discussed at the meeting. "We talked a great deal about family policy," he noted. In Land's view, one of the most important issues right now is population decline. "I would do whatever it takes to reverse that trend," he added.
"The proposal from university rectors and the president of the Academy of Sciences for parliament to consider rector Tiit Land for the presidency is a serious signal both to society and to members of the legislature," Isamaa chair Urmas Reinsalu wrote Tuesday on social media. Reinsalu praised Land's readiness to take on presidential responsibility.
The suggestion for Tallinn University of Technology Rector Tiit Land to run for president was made by the rectors of Estonia's universities, Secretary-General of the Rectors' Council Hanna Kanep and President of the Academy of Sciences Mart Saarma.
"I have thought about this seriously and am ready to run if I am nominated. My long leadership experience and recognition in the education and research field encourage me. I have studied and worked abroad, and international communication is not foreign to me," Land wrote Tuesday on social media.
"Using a chemical term, I am neutral for the presidency. I am not a candidate of any single party. The role of president requires sufficiently broad trust. If members of the Riigikogu find that my experience and values could be useful for Estonia in this role, then I am ready to accept that responsibility," added the current rector of Tallinn University of Technology.
Center Party to form its position after meetings
On Tuesday, the Center Party board met with members of its Riigikogu faction to discuss how to proceed in the presidential election, faction chair Lauri Laats said. They planned to meet with Tiit Land and also wished to speak with Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise.
"We discussed and mapped out where we stand and what possible steps we could take," Laats said. On Wednesday at 15:30 there was a scheduled meeting with Tiit Land. "If additional candidates emerge, we will of course meet with them as well," Laats noted.
Laats said parties have previously met Madise in her role as chancellor of justice, but not as a potential presidential candidate. "We do not know what her vision of the presidency is or how she sees herself in that role," he added.
Once the Center Party chooses its presidential candidate, the party council must be convened. "The board will make a proposal, and the faction will form its position based on that," Laats said. He noted that every Riigikogu member, including Center Party MPs, is free in their vote and will make their decision at the ballot box according to their conscience.
